eligible_types: One Optional wrapper around the listed types
eligible_frames: ROWS with both bounds Preceding, CurrentRow or Following; MIN/MAX argument count exactly one.
source_contracts: Queue rows receive one private partition-local absolute ordinal; the public output layout excludes it.

ROW frame endpoints advance monotonically, by at most one entering row per output after the first nonempty frame. The first frame is folded once; later entry reads use the existing constant-time single-element WinFrame form.
A previous endpoint of zero means no nonempty frame has been seen. Empty frames clear both stacks while retaining the high-water endpoint; clipped tails never insert an already seen row.

Every rear stack entry stores its ordinal, original optional scalar and chronological prefix summary. Transferring newest-to-oldest prepends an entry whose summary combines its raw value before the existing front summary. Final combination places front before rear.
Front expiry compares absolute ordinals against the first current-frame row. Each expired entry is visited once plus one stopping check per output. Front Skip is an O(1) direct-list slice.
Rear lists are only prepended or cleared. A transferred front is only skipped until empty, preventing a Prepend-after-Freezed copy cycle.

TListRepresentation copying transfers its Normal capability; HolderFactory Prepend preserves this transfer and uses geometric NewNormal growth. Head, length and direct-list iterator reads do not copy that representation.

Scalar MIN/MAX implementations select an existing value under a total order. Integer/date/interval ties have identical scalar bits; Decimal compares raw 128-bit encodings. Optional absence is the aggregate identity.
No aggregate arithmetic is regrouped by this amendment. Floating, composite, opaque, string/timezone and unlisted data slots retain existing behavior.
The final per-frame Fold1 omits only these eligible MIN/MAX definitions; other aggregate families and RANGE keep the previous path.

The input queue stores ordinary cumulative rows plus an ordinal, never persistent stack snapshots. Two-stack memory is bounded by the largest admitted ROWS frame, with geometric backing-buffer overhead.
remaining_open: RANGE MIN/MAX entering batches are not exposed by the allowed WinFrame API. Incremental handles return only the last boundary row.
QueueRange/QueuePeek are rejected when WindowNewPipeline is enabled, which is its default. Skip over WinFrame would walk the skipped rows because TQueueRange lacks SkipListImpl.
Unbounded-frame MIN/MAX and excluded value families retain existing paths; this is not complete MIN/MAX closure.
Floating/Decimal/Interval SUM and AVG remain outside this amendment.
native_required: Compile/type-annotate anonymous generated plans against this exact source branch.
Required/optional/all-null scalar MIN/MAX, both functions together, and mixed COUNT/integer SUM/fallback aggregates.
Leading/trailing empty frames, clipped boundaries, current/following/preceding offsets, both sort directions, peer rows, multiple partitions and downstream filtering.
Private ordinal and stack fields cannot appear in the public result schema.
No reachable per-frame Fold1 for eligible MIN/MAX-only plans; Fold is allowed only for initial entry and one-time rear transfer.
Measure operations/allocations at fixed row count versus width and fixed width versus row count after all peephole passes.
Verify persistent-list storage remains bounded by frame width and input queue lookahead rather than total partition rows.

kqp_owned_runtime_extension_assessment.limitation: A new RANGE-delta callable would need its own type/compiler/runtime contract and safe access to collector queue state. The current queue resource implementation is private to essentials; duplicating its layout or bypassing its deprecation checks is not a sound extension. A KQP-owned stream window operator could instead own collection and aggregation, but that expands scope materially and requires dedicated runtime validation.
